bullets.title: S&P 500 logs 7-day losing streak — worst week since April 2025
bullets.body: The S&P 500 posted seven consecutive daily declines (Dow -8.02%, S&P -8.61%, Nasdaq -10.02%, Russell -7.48%), the longest streak since February 2020. The SOX semiconductor index fell 17.1% over the period, its sixth weekly decline in seven weeks. Breadth was extreme: S&P decliners outnumbered gainers 15:1 and 68% of global equity market indices are now oversold per BofA. The S&P is now roughly flat YTD after peaking up ~18.7% from an October ATH.

bullets.title: Fed hawkishness is the macro driver — Waller signals 50bp December hike
bullets.body: Governor Waller and multiple Fed speakers hardened rhetoric this week, with Waller floating a 50bp December hike and advocating for reversal of 2025's risk-management cuts. FOMC minutes showed almost all participants judged further hikes appropriate. The market is now pricing ~62bp of additional hikes over 10 months. Real 2-year yields rose 73bp over 13 weeks. Multiple strategists note the Fed has shifted from growth-management to inflation-credibility mode — meaning the traditional Fed put may not engage on equity/credit stress alone. Core PCE is tracking 3.22% y/y for October; Morgan Stanley forecasts 25bp hikes in December and March, then a hold.

bullets.title: AI trade in full bear market — NVDA down 47% from ATH despite beat/raise
bullets.body: NVDA extended its decline to -47% from all-time highs even after reporting a strong Q3 ($115.8B revenue, +103% y/y) and raising FY28 guidance to ~75% growth. Headwinds include: SEC civil probe into potential accounting issues, halt of Hopper/H200 shipments to China (~$2.4B in quarterly revenue removed), new BIS export controls requiring licenses for chip sales to Malaysia, Singapore, Indonesia, Thailand and Brazil, and leadership uncertainty (board ruled out Jensen Huang's return). The AI infrastructure index (MSXXAI) fell -15% w/w and -46% from ATHs. UBS cut its 2028 EPS estimate to ~$18.80 and PT to $220 (from $240–$300 range at various houses).

bullets.title: US-China chip export controls tighten materially — SE Asia loophole closed
bullets.body: The Commerce Department issued an interim final rule restricting remote access to US advanced AI chips by companies affiliated with Country Group D:5 or Macau; licenses now required for chip exports to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Brazil. TSMC and Samsung halted consumer chip shipments to Chinese customers (16nm and below) pending US license approvals. BABA warned new rules will affect 2027 products and pivoted to in-house T-Head chips. UBS estimates the controls could strip 1-2 GW from AI chip demand. The MATCH Act and Chip Security Act are odds-on for NDAA inclusion, potentially restricting ASML DUV tools to China.

bullets.title: Hedge fund positioning hits multi-year lows — semis most sold sector for 6 weeks
bullets.body: Fundamental L/S hedge funds were down ~1.5% on the day Friday and -4% MTD, with 5-day returns below -3 sigma. HF net leverage fell from 12-month highs to the 26th percentile over five years; Equity L/S is at the 21st percentile globally. Semis are the most net-sold US group over the past two months, with the six-week selling streak in semis the longest on record. HFs are now net short US momentum for the first time since April 2025. Goldman Sachs estimates $57B in CTA selling over the last month. Retail was a net buyer of ~$29B in US equities despite the drawdown.

bullets.title: Tech sector rotation into defensives at dot-com bust levels
bullets.body: Rotation out of Tech into Utilities, Telecom, Pharma/Biotech, Real Estate, and Consumer Staples accelerated to levels not seen since the dot-com bust. Consumer Staples Distribution & Retail positioning reached historical highs. XLP now trades at a ~15% premium to the S&P 500, the widest gap since December 2022. Homebuilders and utilities look expensive relative to current rate levels despite defensive rotation. Morgan Stanley QDS recommends selling skew given the SPX Put/Call Vol spread (25-delta, 3M/1Y) is at its highest reading below 10% of time since 2013, historically yielding +3.6% returns over 2 months.

bullets.title: Data center permitting headwinds multiply — TX freeze, Loudoun pause, Trump tax threat
bullets.body: Multiple simultaneous regulatory shocks hit AI infrastructure: Texas Governor-elect Hinojosa announced a data center permit moratorium; Loudoun County (VA) adopted a 12-month pause; Arizona AG sought delay of SpaceX's $50B campus hearing; North Carolina Governor called for phasing out data center subsidies; Trump announced a policy banning US companies from building data centers abroad with tax penalties. These actions collectively threaten 30%+ of GW pipeline in 2028 per SemiAnalysis. Meanwhile, Texas TCEQ resumed air permits for existing projects after a prior freeze. The BIS rule requiring overseas data centers to perform due diligence on high-risk customers adds further regulatory burden.

bullets.title: Cross-asset signals confirm risk-off regime: dollar up, gold/copper/Bitcoin all crashed
bullets.body: Gold fell 9.5% (worst week since March), silver -16.4%, copper -9.9% (sixth consecutive weekly decline, -4.3 standard deviations), WTI crude -5.8%. Bitcoin futures fell 15.5% (seventh straight week lower) to near June two-year lows, hitting ~$58K. The dollar index reached 52-week highs. Real yields gapped higher as inflation expectations fell faster than nominal yields. 22V's cross-asset risk monitor registered a rare signal: S&P, Russell, and NDX all closed below 200-day MAs while the 10-year yield was above its 50- and 200-day MAs — this combination has occurred only six times since 2008.

bullets.title: Treasuries rallied as safe haven; 2Y yield fell 24bp, 20Y auction solid
bullets.body: Treasuries re-established flight-to-quality behavior. The 2-year yield fell 24bp to ~4.61% and the 10-year fell ~14bp to ~4.91% over the week. The 20-year auction stopped on the screws with solid foreign participation. Pensions and asset allocators are forecast to buy ~$50B at current prices (SPX -3%) per MS QDS. JPMorgan forecasts 2027 Treasury demand of ~$1.38T, noting a bill-heavy mix reduces duration pressure despite a widening supply/demand gap.

bullets.title: Anthropic (ANT) IPO: largest ever at $81.3B raised, priced $83, opened $111 then retreated
bullets.body: Anthropic priced at $83/share (above the $70-78 range), raising a record $81.3B on ~980M shares sold, with ~7x oversubscription and a fully diluted valuation of ~$1.5T. The stock opened at $111.50 but fell back toward the IPO price by Friday — consistent with historical patterns where large IPOs typically decline 30-50% in their first year. Wolfe Research initiated with Outperform and $135 PT (63% upside) projecting revenue of $53B/135B/280B for 2026E/27E/28E. The IPO validates AI capex spend but also creates supply pressure; slowing data-center buildout post-midterms is viewed as bullish for Google/Meta FCF.

bullets.title: FOMC minutes hawkish; MS, JPM see 25bp hikes in Dec and Mar, then hold
bullets.body: October FOMC minutes showed 'almost all participants' see further hikes as appropriate. Fedspeak this week (Waller, Musalem, Logan, Daly, Barr, Paulson) was uniformly hawkish. Morgan Stanley forecasts 25bp hikes in December and March to 4.25–4.50%, then a hold through 2027 and easing in 2028. JPMorgan's Mike Feroli forecasts three hikes (Dec/Jan/Mar) to 4.5–4.75% with core PCE remaining in mid-to-high 2% range. The key risk: Fed is now willing to tolerate slower economic growth to reach the 2% inflation target — a shift from the past five years of risk-management approach.

bullets.title: Consumer resilient — October retail sales beat, control group +0.6% m/m
bullets.body: October control-group retail sales came in at +0.6% m/m versus +0.3% consensus; prior months were revised up 70bp. Morgan Stanley raised 4Q real PCE tracking to 2.1% q/q annualized from 1.6%. BofA data shows holiday spending off to a strong start with spending growth converging across income groups. Goldman Sachs estimates the S&P 500 is pricing in negative semis EPS growth after 2027 at current valuations — a disconnect given the strong consumer backdrop. The Atlanta Fed GDPNow tracker is at 3.4% for Q4, well above economic speed limits.

bullets.title: Housing at cycle lows — NAHB falls to 14-year low, pending sales at record low
bullets.body: November NAHB homebuilder sentiment dropped to 25, the lowest since 2012. October pending home sales missed badly at -4.7% m/m (consensus -1.8%), hitting an all-time low. Building permits fell 8.9% m/m, the second consecutive soft month. Existing home sales are tracking toward 3.6M annualized, the lowest since 2010. Mortgage rates rose to 7.28-7.35%. Morgan Stanley revised Q4 residential investment tracking to -6.0% q/q ar from prior +1.0%.

bullets.title: Geopolitical escalation: Ukraine destroys Kerch Bridge; Trump-Xi-Putin Shenzhen summit
bullets.body: Ukraine destroyed the Kerch Bridge (a major military/logistics victory), triggering Russian missile and drone retaliation including strikes in neighboring Poland. Trump dismissed the Polish strikes as 'a couple of little missiles, by mistake.' The EU is discussing an additional €45B in Ukraine aid. Separately, Trump, Xi, and Putin met at APEC in Shenzhen, producing a declaration that makes no reference to Ukraine but commits the three powers to increase refined petroleum production. This would be detrimental to Russia's war effort. Geopolitical risk also includes rising US-Iran tensions (additional $8B in US strikes on Iran sites) and escalating cyber security incidents across major tech platforms.

bullets.title: AI users outperforming non-AI peers on productivity and margin expectations
bullets.body: S&P 1500 companies with clear AI usage show accelerating sales-per-employee growth and improving forward net margin expectations, while non-AI user forward margins are declining. Approximately 50% of S&P 1500 companies now use AI, up from 20% in 2024. 22V Research and Goldman Sachs Quant both recommend staying long high-AI-usage companies (non-software services, manufacturers) as the clearest way to express AI adoption without direct infrastructure exposure. Narrowly defined AI explains 22% of aggregate demand growth YTD; broadly defined AI explains 42%.

bullets.title: Goldman raises S&P 500 2027 target to 8,700; Morgan Stanley to 8,700 as well
bullets.body: Both Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley raised their year-end 2027 S&P 500 targets to 8,700 (17-18% upside from current levels), based on 18-19x forward EPS of ~$420-458. The bull case rests on intact AI capex cycle, healthy EPS growth (14-18% in 2027 vs ~30-34% in 2026), lower oil, and broadening AI adoption beyond infrastructure. The bear case requires 2028 AI capex disappoint (SemiAnalysis cut 2028 AI accelerator spend by 28%) and monetary tightening exceeding current forecasts. JPMorgan's SPX year-end target remains 8,000 (8.4% upside at current levels).

bullets.title: EM and global macro: Japan BOJ tightening expected; eurozone facing more difficult 2027
bullets.body: The BOJ is expected to hike in December with March follow-up brought forward, as Japan's nominal exports surged +21.1% y/y driven by price inflation. The eurozone faces a more challenging 2027 after a resilient 2026, with energy prices, tighter credit, and political uncertainty weighing. JPMorgan expects two further ECB hikes (December 2026, March 2027). Euro-area consumer confidence edged up to -16.9 in November but remains 1.5 standard deviations below long-run average. UK core CPI undershot BoE forecasts at 2.8% y/y, reducing urgency for a December hike — JPM sticks with February timing.

bullets.title: CrowdStrike in talks to acquire Zscaler — ZS +18% after-hours
bullets.body: Bloomberg reported that CrowdStrike is in acquisition talks with Zscaler. ZS shares surged 18% in after-hours trading on the news. No terms were disclosed. The deal, if completed, would create a dominant consolidated cybersecurity platform combining endpoint, network, and cloud security.

bullets.title: Semiconductor supply chain: Taiwan/Korea export orders at records but shipments peaking
bullets.body: Taiwan October export orders rose +78.3% y/y to record highs, with US orders to Taiwan +96.3% y/y to a record $44.9B. However, actual shipment growth is peaking and faces hard comps. PSC Macro warns orders may be inflated by double-ordering similar to 1990s patterns. Semiconductor sales growth is expected to slow from 2026's 108% y/y to just 29% in 2027. Korea's semiconductor export business confidence is clearly declining. MSCI All World IT index growth decelerated from 69% y/y in June to 16% currently.
